## Tokyo Business Trip at a Glance
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

A 3-day plan centered on **Tokyo Station** keeps commute time low and makes room for client dinners plus sightseeing.
Budget target of **USD 1,800 total excluding flights** is achievable with a mid-range business hotel, train/subway transit, and a few polished meals.

## Day-by-Day Tokyo Schedule
### Day 1: Tue, 2026-04-14 — Arrival, Meeting, Client Dinner
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg

- **07:00–09:00** Arrival and transfer to hotel near Tokyo Station
  - Transit: **Narita Express** or **Airport Limousine Bus** if arriving from NRT; **Keikyu/Monorail + JR** if arriving from HND.
  - Check-in goal: leave bags at the hotel if rooms are not ready.
- **09:30–12:00** Business meeting
  - Transit suggestion: walk or 1–2 stops by JR/subway if the office is in Marunouchi, Otemachi, Nihonbashi, or Ginza.
- **12:15–13:15** Lunch
  - Good fit: set lunch at **Tokyo Station Yaesu/Marunouchi** area, or a quick bento if the meeting runs long.
- **13:30–16:00** Free time for sightseeing
  - Best nearby options: **Tokyo Station Marunouchi Building**, **Imperial Palace East Gardens**, or **Ginza**.
- **16:00–17:30** Reset at hotel / prep for dinner
  - Transit: short taxi or train back to hotel to change.
- **18:30–20:30** Client dinner
  - Recommendation: a private room or upscale izakaya in **Ginza**, **Marunouchi**, or **Nihonbashi**.
  - Meal style: course menu or seasonal kaiseki for a polished business setting.
- **20:30–21:30** Optional evening walk
  - Easy choice: **Tokyo Station illumination** or **Ginza night streets**.

### Day 2: Wed, 2026-04-15 — Meeting, Sightseeing Block, Client Dinner
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock.svg

- **07:30–08:30** Breakfast and commute buffer
  - Transit: walk if staying in Marunouchi/Yaesu; otherwise use JR Yamanote, Tokyo Metro, or a taxi for punctuality.
- **09:30–12:00** Business meeting
  - Keep a 15-minute buffer for security, elevator time, and coffee.
- **12:00–13:00** Lunch
  - Recommendation: soba, tempura set, or a business lunch near the meeting venue.
- **13:15–16:00** Free time for sightseeing
  - Best options for a compact block: **Asakusa and Senso-ji**, **Ueno Park**, or **Akihabara** depending on your interests.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/31/2014_02_08_ueno.jpg Alt=Best options for a compact block: **Asakusa and Senso-ji**, **Ueno Park**, or **Akihabara** depending on your interests, Tokyo, Japan
- **16:00–17:30** Return to hotel / refresh
  - Transit: subway or JR back toward Tokyo Station.
- **18:30–20:30** Client dinner
  - Recommendation: **Ginza** sushi, yakiniku, or a modern Japanese restaurant with reservations.
- **20:30–21:30** Optional short nightlife stop
  - Easy choice: **Marunouchi Naka-dori** or a dessert stop near Tokyo Station.

### Day 3: Thu, 2026-04-16 — Wrap-Up, Flexible Work, Departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/suitcase.svg

- **08:00–09:00** Breakfast and checkout prep
  - Pack documents, chargers, and receipts before leaving the room.
- **09:00–11:00** Buffer for email, calls, or last business task
  - Transit: stay near Tokyo Station for easy logistics.
- **11:00–13:30** Sightseeing block
  - Best nearby choices: **Imperial Palace area**, **Nihonbashi**, **Tsukiji Outer Market**, or a final shopping run in **Tokyo Station**.
- **13:30–15:00** Lunch and hotel pickup
  - Recommendation: final Japanese meal near the station for easy departure.
- **15:00 onward** Airport transfer or onward travel
  - Transit: allow extra time for rush-hour congestion if heading to the airport.

## Budget Plan for 2 Adults
### Estimated Spend Within USD 1,800
| Category | Planned Spend | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hotel, 3 nights | USD 900–1,150 | Business hotel near Tokyo Station, twin or king room |
| Local transit | USD 60–120 | JR/subway/taxi mix for short business hops |
| Breakfasts | USD 45–90 | Hotel breakfast or nearby cafés |
| Lunches | USD 90–150 | 3 days, mid-range set meals |
| Client dinners | USD 360–540 | 3 dinners, polished but controlled spend |
| Sightseeing / coffee / snacks | USD 80–150 | Light discretionary spend |
| Buffer | USD 100–200 | Tips, luggage storage, extras |
| **Total** | **USD 1,635–2,400** | To stay under budget, target hotel near the lower-middle range and cap dinners |

### Budget-Control Tips
- Choose a hotel in **Marunouchi, Yaesu, or Nihonbashi** to reduce taxi use.
- Book client dinners with a **set course budget** in advance.
- Use **train + walk** for daytime movement; reserve taxis for late dinners or rain.

## Hotel and Transit Strategy Near Tokyo Station
### Best Stay Area
- **Marunouchi / Yaesu**: closest to Tokyo Station, best for business convenience.
- **Nihonbashi**: often slightly better value, still very convenient.
- **Ginza**: strong dining and client-entertainment options, but usually pricier.

### Transit Suggestions
- **Airport to hotel**: Narita Express or limousine bus from NRT; monorail/Keikyu from HND.
- **Daily meetings**: walk if within 15 minutes; otherwise Tokyo Metro or JR.
- **Client dinners**: pre-book taxis for punctual arrival if the venue is in Ginza/Shibuya/Roppongi.

## Simple Packing Checklist
### Business Travel Essentials
- Passport / ID
- Meeting notes, business cards, charger, power bank
- Laptop, cable, adapter, mouse if needed
- 3 days of business attire plus one backup shirt/blouse
- Comfortable walking shoes
- Compact umbrella
- Toiletries and any medication
- Expense card / cash for transit and small purchases
- Receipts folder or phone photo folder for expense tracking
